title: Fund the most value within one budget

expected.says: Run's report for the demo export matches the expected report

blueprint.contract: Takes a Request. Returns a Built holding a MathOpt model with one binary variable per project (named `x_<id>`), one row named budget that keeps the summed capex of the funded projects within capital_budget, and the summed value of the funded projects as the objective to maximize.
blueprint.idea: A yes-or-no choice per project under one budget is a 0-1 knapsack: the best fill is a combination, which no sort by value per dollar finds in general.

blueprint.contract: Solves the model with HiGHS through MathOpt, on one thread, and returns the SolveResult. Nothing HiGHS prints may reach the program's standard output.
blueprint.idea: The solver is a call with parameters; its log is not the planner's report.

blueprint.signature: def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: Turns a SolveResult into a Plan: the status in lower case, each project whose variable is 1 mapped to its earliest start year, and the objective value. With no feasible solution, a Plan with the status alone.
blueprint.idea: Read the termination first, then the variable values; a binary is 1 when its value is above 0.5.

lesson.title: 4.2.2 Reading `SolveResult`: Termination, Primal and Dual Solutions, Statistics

blueprint.contract: Builds the model for a Request, solves it and returns the Plan.
blueprint.idea: Keep building, solving and reading back in separate functions, so each can be tested and changed alone.

lesson.title: 14.2.1 The First Request: Fund Projects Within One Budget

cases: the funded projects cost no more than the budget
the plan is the best combination, not the best value per dollar taken in order
every project is funded when the budget holds them all
the report counts the funded projects and totals their capex and value
the command line plans the export file it is given
